1500.title: Credential Validation
1500.description: Auditing credential validation events (both success and failure) provides critical information about logon attempts, including potential brute-force attacks or unauthorized access attempts.Configure the "Credential Validation" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Account Logon).

1501.title: Security Group Management
1501.description: Auditing successful security group management events helps track changes to group memberships, which is important for maintaining access control and detecting unauthorized modifications.Configure the "Security Group Management" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Account Management).

1502.title: User Account Management
1502.description: Auditing user account management events (both success and failure) provides a comprehensive record of account creation, modification, and deletion, which is vital for security monitoring and compliance.Configure the "User Account Management" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Account Management).

1503.title: DPAPI Activity
1503.description: Auditing DPAPI (Data Protection API) activity (both success and failure) helps monitor access to encrypted data and credentials, which can be crucial for detecting attempts to compromise sensitive information.Configure the "DPAPI Activity" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> System).

1504.title: Plug and Play Events
1504.description: Auditing successful Plug and Play events helps track the installation and removal of hardware devices, which can be important for detecting unauthorized device usage or potential data exfiltration.Configure the "Plug and Play Events" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> System).

1505.title: Process Creation
1505.description: Auditing successful process creation events provides valuable insights into program execution on the system, which can help detect malware activity or unauthorized software installations.Configure the "Process Creation" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Detailed Tracking).

1506.title: Account Lockout
1506.description: Auditing account lockout failures helps identify potential brute-force attacks against user accounts, allowing administrators to respond quickly to suspicious activity.Configure the "Account Lockout" audit subcategory to "Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Account Logon).

1507.title: Group Membership
1507.description: Auditing successful group membership events helps track changes to user and group memberships, which is important for maintaining access control and detecting unauthorized modifications.Configure the "Group Membership" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Account Logon).

1508.title: Logon
1508.description: Auditing both successful and failed logon events is fundamental for security monitoring, providing a complete record of who is accessing the system and when, as well as attempts by unauthorized users.Configure the "Logon" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Logon/Logoff).

1509.title: Other Logon/Logoff Events
1509.description: Auditing other logon/logoff events (both success and failure) provides additional context for user session activity, which can be useful for detecting unusual behavior or session hijacking attempts.Configure the "Other Logon/Logoff Events" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Logon/Logoff).

1510.title: Special Logon
1510.description: Auditing successful special logon events (e.g., logons with administrative privileges) provides critical information about high-privilege activity, which is essential for detecting potential abuse or compromise.Configure the "Special Logon" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Logon/Logoff).

1511.title: Detailed File Share
1511.description: Auditing detailed file share failures provides granular information about unsuccessful attempts to access shared resources, which can help identify unauthorized access attempts or misconfigurations.Configure the "Detailed File Share" audit subcategory to "Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1512.title: File Share
1512.description: Auditing file share events (both success and failure) provides a record of access to shared folders and files, which is important for data security and compliance.Configure the "File Share" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1513.title: Kernel Object
1513.description: Auditing kernel object access events (both success and failure) provides insights into low-level system interactions, which can be useful for detecting advanced persistent threats or rootkit activity.Configure the "Kernel Object" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1514.title: Other Object Access Events
1514.description: Auditing other object access events (both success and failure) provides a broad overview of access attempts to various system objects, which can help detect unusual or unauthorized activity.Configure the "Other Object Access Events" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1515.title: Removable Storage
1515.description: Auditing removable storage events (both success and failure) helps track the use of USB drives and other removable media, which is important for preventing data exfiltration and malware introduction.Configure the "Removable Storage" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1516.title: SAM
1516.description: Auditing SAM (Security Account Manager) events (both success and failure) provides a record of access to the local user and group database, which is important for detecting attempts to enumerate or modify local accounts.Configure the "SAM" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Object Access).

1517.title: Audit Policy Change
1517.description: Auditing successful audit policy changes helps ensure that any modifications to the system's auditing configuration are tracked, preventing an attacker from disabling auditing to cover their tracks.Configure the "Audit Policy Change" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Policy Change).

1518.title: Authentication Policy Change
1518.description: Auditing successful authentication policy changes helps track modifications to authentication-related settings, which is important for maintaining secure authentication mechanisms.Configure the "Authentication Policy Change" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Policy Change).

1519.title: MPSSVC Rule-Level Policy Change
1519.description: Auditing MPSSVC (Microsoft Protection Service) rule-level policy changes (both success and failure) helps track modifications to Windows Firewall rules, which is important for maintaining network security.Configure the "MPSSVC Rule-Level Policy Change" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Policy Change).

1520.title: Other Policy Change Events
1520.description: Auditing other policy change failures provides a broad overview of unsuccessful attempts to modify system policies, which can help detect unauthorized configuration changes.Configure the "Other Policy Change Events" audit subcategory to "Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Policy Change).

1521.title: Sensitive Privilege Use
1521.description: Auditing sensitive privilege use events (both success and failure) provides critical information about the exercise of powerful user rights, which is essential for detecting potential privilege escalation or abuse.Configure the "Sensitive Privilege Use" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> Privilege Use).

1522.title: Other System Events
1522.description: Auditing other system events (both success and failure) provides a broad overview of system-level activities, which can be useful for detecting unusual behavior or system health issues.Configure the "Other System Events" audit subcategory to "Success and Failure" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> System).

1523.title: Security State Change
1523.description: Auditing successful security state changes helps track modifications to the system's security configuration, ensuring that any unauthorized changes are detected.Configure the "Security State Change" audit subcategory to "Success" in Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Windows Settings -> Security Settings -> Advanced Audit Policy Configuration -> System).

1524.title: Security System Extension
1524.description: This check verifies if auditing for 'Security System Extension' events is configured. By default, no auditing is performed. It is recommended to audit successful events to track security-related system extensions and potential misuse. To resolve, configure the advanced audit policy for 'Security System Extension' to include 'Success' events using `auditpol /set /subcategory:{0CCE9211-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030} /success:enable`.

1525.title: System Integrity
1525.description: This check verifies if auditing for 'System Integrity' events is configured. It is recommended to audit both successful and failed events to ensure the integrity of the system and detect any tampering attempts. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the advanced audit policy for 'System Integrity' is configured to include 'Success and Failure' events using `auditpol /set /subcategory:{0CCE9212-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030} /success:enable /failure:enable`.

1600.title: Personalization: Prevent enabling lock screen camera
1600.description: This check verifies if the camera can be enabled on the lock screen. By default, it might be enabled (0), which could pose a privacy risk. It is recommended to prevent the camera from being enabled on the lock screen (1). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Personalization\NoLockScreenCamera` to `1`.

1601.title: DNS Client: Turn off multicast name resolution (LLMNR)
1601.description: This check verifies if Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR) is disabled. LLMNR is a protocol that can be exploited for name resolution spoofing attacks. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to disable LLMNR (0) for enhanced security. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient\EnableMulticast` to `0`.

1602.title: Lanman Workstation: Enable insecure guest logons
1602.description: This check verifies if insecure guest logons are disabled for the Lanman Workstation service. Enabling insecure guest logons (1) can allow unauthenticated access to shared resources, posing a significant security risk. It is recommended to disable insecure guest logons (0). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\LanmanWorkstation\AllowInsecureGuestAuth` to `0`.

1603.title: Turn off Microsoft Peer-to-Peer Networking Services
1603.description: This check verifies if Microsoft Peer-to-Peer Networking Services are turned off. These services, if enabled (0), can create direct connections between computers, potentially bypassing network security controls. It is recommended to disable these services (1) unless specifically required. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\policies\Microsoft\Peernet\Disabled` to `1`.

1604.title: WLAN Settings: Allow Windows to automatically connect to suggested open hotspots, to networks shared by contacts, and to hotspots offering paid services
1604.description: This check verifies if Windows is prevented from automatically connecting to suggested open hotspots, networks shared by contacts, and paid hotspots. Allowing automatic connections (1) can expose the system to untrusted networks and potential security threats. It is recommended to disable this feature (0). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\wcmsvc\wifinetworkmanager\config\AutoConnectAllowedOEM` to `0`.

2108.title: Turn on PowerShell Module Logging
2108.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Module Logging is enabled. Module logging (1) records pipeline execution details for PowerShell modules, which is crucial for security monitoring and incident response. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ModuleLogging\EnableModuleLogging` to `1`.

2109.title: Turn on PowerShell Module Logging (PowerShell Policy)
2109.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Module Logging is configured to use the Windows PowerShell policy setting. Enabling this (1) ensures that module logging adheres to the system-wide PowerShell policy, providing consistent logging for security analysis. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ModuleLogging\UseWindowsPowerShellPolicySetting` to `1`.

2110.title: Turn on PowerShell Module Logging - Module Names
2110.description: This check verifies if specific module names are configured for PowerShell Module Logging. It is recommended to log all modules (`*`) or a comprehensive list of critical modules to ensure full visibility into PowerShell activity for security monitoring. To resolve, ensure the multi-string registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ModuleLogging\ModuleNames` contains `*` or a list of all modules to be logged.

2111.title: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging
2111.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Script Block Logging is enabled. Script block logging (1) records the content of PowerShell commands as they are executed, which is essential for detecting malicious scripts and for forensic analysis. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ScriptBlockLogging\EnableScriptBlockLogging` to `1`.

2112.title: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging (Invocation)
2112.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Script Block Invocation Logging is enabled. Invocation logging (1) records the start and end of script block invocations, providing additional context for script execution analysis. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ScriptBlockLogging\EnableScriptBlockInvocationLogging` to `1`.

2113.title: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging (PowerShell Policy)
2113.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Script Block Logging is configured to use the Windows PowerShell policy setting. Enabling this (1) ensures that script block logging adheres to the system-wide PowerShell policy, providing consistent logging for security analysis. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\ScriptBlockLogging\UseWindowsPowerShellPolicySetting` to `1`.

2116.title: Turn on PowerShell Transcription
2116.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Transcription is enabled. Transcription (1) records all input and output of PowerShell sessions, creating a detailed log of user activity, which is invaluable for security auditing and incident investigation. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\Transcription\EnableTranscripting` to `1`.

2114.title: Turn on PowerShell Transcription (Invocation)
2114.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Transcription includes invocation headers. Enabling invocation headers (1) provides additional context in transcription logs, making it easier to trace the origin and sequence of PowerShell commands. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\Transcription\EnableInvocationHeader` to `1`.

2115.title: Turn on PowerShell Transcription (PowerShell Policy)
2115.description: This check verifies if PowerShell Transcription is configured to use the Windows PowerShell policy setting. Enabling this (1) ensures that transcription adheres to the system-wide PowerShell policy, providing consistent logging for security analysis. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PowerShellCore\Transcription\UseWindowsPowerShellPolicySetting` to `1`.

1772.title: Configure Redirection Guard
1772.description: This check verifies if Redirection Guard for printers is configured. Redirection Guard (1) helps protect against printer redirection vulnerabilities by restricting which print servers can redirect print jobs. It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\RedirectionGuardPolicy` to `1`.

1768.title: Only use Package Point and Print (CVE-2021-36958)
1768.description: This check verifies if the system is configured to only use Package Point and Print, which is a more secure method for installing printer drivers and helps mitigate CVE-2021-36958. It is recommended to enable this setting (1) to enhance printer security. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PackagePointAndPrint\PackagePointAndPrintOnly` to `1`.

1769.title: Package Point and Print - Approved servers (CVE-2021-36958)
1769.description: This check verifies if Package Point and Print is configured to restrict connections to approved print servers, which helps mitigate CVE-2021-36958. It is recommended to enable this policy (1) and specify a list of trusted print servers to prevent connections to malicious or unapproved servers. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PackagePointAndPrint\PackagePointAndPrintServerList` to `1` (to enable the policy) and populate the list of approved servers.

1764.title: Point and Print Restrictions: When installing drivers for a new connection (CVE-2021-34527)
1764.description: This check ensures that Point and Print restrictions are properly configured to prevent automatic driver installation without warnings or elevation prompts when connecting to new printers. This addresses a critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527). It is recommended to require warnings and elevation prompts for new printer driver installations (0 for `NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall`). The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint\NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall` is set to `0`.

1765.title: Point and Print Restrictions: When updating drivers for an existing connection (CVE-2021-34527)
1765.description: This check ensures that Point and Print restrictions are properly configured to prevent automatic driver updates without warnings or elevation prompts for existing printer connections. This addresses a critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-34527). It is recommended to require warnings and elevation prompts for printer driver updates (0 for `UpdatePromptSettings`). The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint\UpdatePromptSettings` is set to `0`.

1771.category: Administrative Templates: Start Menu and Taskbar
1771.title: Notifications: Turn off notifications network usage
1771.description: This check verifies if notifications are prevented from using network resources. Disabling network usage for notifications (1) can reduce potential data leakage and improve privacy. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off notifications network usage. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\PushNotifications\NoCloudApplicationNotification` to `1`.

1605.title: Credentials Delegation: Allow delegation default credentials
1605.description: This check verifies if the delegation of default credentials is disabled. Allowing default credentials delegation (1) can expose user credentials to remote servers, increasing the risk of credential theft and lateral movement. It is recommended to disable this feature (0). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CredentialsDelegation\AllowDefaultCredentials` to `0`.

1606.title: Credentials Delegation: Encryption Oracle Remediation
1606.description: This check verifies if the CredSSP Encryption Oracle Remediation policy is configured to a secure level. Setting it to 'Force Updated Clients' or 'Mitigated' (0) protects against known vulnerabilities in the Credential Security Support Provider protocol. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\CredSSP\Parameters\AllowEncryptionOracle` is set to `0`.

1699.title: Credentials Delegation: Remote host allows delegation of non-exportable credentials
1699.description: This check verifies if the delegation of non-exportable credentials to remote hosts is prevented. Allowing this (0) could potentially expose sensitive credentials. It is recommended to prevent remote hosts from allowing delegation of non-exportable credentials (1). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CredentialsDelegation\AllowProtectedCreds` to `1`.

1607.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices that match an ID
1607.description: This check verifies if the installation of devices matching specific IDs is prevented. Enabling this restriction (1) enhances security by preventing unauthorized hardware from being installed. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceIDs` to `1`.

1608.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices that match an ID (Retroactive)
1608.description: This check verifies if the installation of devices matching specific IDs is retroactively prevented. Enabling this restriction (1) ensures that even previously installed devices matching a denied ID are blocked, enhancing security. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceIDsRetroactive` to `1`.

1609.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices that match ID PCI\CC_0C0010 (Firewire)
1609.description: This check verifies if the installation of Firewire (PCI\\CC_0C0010) devices is prevented. Firewire ports can be used for direct memory access (DMA) attacks, allowing attackers to bypass security controls. It is recommended to prevent the installation of Firewire devices. To resolve, ensure `PCI\CC_0C0010` is added to the multi-string registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceIDs`.

1610.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices that match ID PCI\CC_0C0A (Thunderbolt)
1610.description: This check verifies if the installation of Thunderbolt (PCI\\CC_0C0A) devices is prevented. Thunderbolt ports can be used for direct memory access (DMA) attacks, allowing attackers to bypass security controls. It is recommended to prevent the installation of Thunderbolt devices. To resolve, ensure `PCI\CC_0C0A` is added to the multi-string registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceIDs`.

1611.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices using drivers that match an device setup class
1611.description: This check verifies if the installation of devices using drivers that match a specific device setup class is prevented. Enabling this restriction (1) enhances security by preventing unauthorized device types from being installed. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceClasses` to `1`.

1612.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices using drivers that match an device setup class (Retroactive)
1612.description: This check verifies if the installation of devices using drivers that match a specific device setup class is retroactively prevented. Enabling this restriction (1) ensures that even previously installed devices matching a denied class are blocked, enhancing security. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceClassesRetroactive` to `1`.

1613.title: Device Installation: Device Installation Restrictions: Prevent installation of devices using drivers that match d48179be-ec20-11d1-b6b8-00c04fa372a7 (SBP-2 drive)
1613.description: This check verifies if the installation of SBP-2 (d48179be-ec20-11d1-b6b8-00c04fa372a7) drives is prevented. SBP-2 devices can be used for direct memory access (DMA) attacks, allowing attackers to bypass security controls. It is recommended to prevent the installation of SBP-2 drives. To resolve, ensure `d48179be-ec20-11d1-b6b8-00c04fa372a7` is added to the multi-string registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceInstall\Restrictions\DenyDeviceClasses`.

1614.title: Device Guard: Virtualization Based Security Status
1614.description: This check verifies the status of Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) for Device Guard. VBS (status 2 indicates running) provides critical protection by isolating sensitive processes and data. It is recommended that VBS is enabled and running. To resolve, ensure VBS is enabled and configured through Group Policy or system settings (e.g., 'Turn On Virtualization Based Security' policy).

1615.title: Device Guard: Available Security Properties: Secure Boot
1615.description: This check verifies if Secure Boot is an available security property for Device Guard. Secure Boot (value 2) helps ensure that only trusted software can load during startup, preventing rootkits and other low-level malware. It is recommended that Secure Boot is available. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure Secure Boot is enabled in the UEFI/BIOS settings of the system.

1616.title: Device Guard: Available Security Properties: DMA protection
1616.description: This check verifies if DMA protection is an available security property for Device Guard. DMA protection (value 3) safeguards against attacks that attempt to access system memory directly via peripheral devices. It is recommended that DMA protection is available. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure Kernel DMA Protection is enabled in system settings or Group Policy.

1617.title: Device Guard: Security Services Configured: Credential Guard
1617.description: This check verifies if Credential Guard is configured as a security service for Device Guard. Credential Guard (value 1) uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets, preventing credential theft attacks. It is recommended that Credential Guard is configured. To resolve, enable Credential Guard through Group Policy or system settings.

1619.title: Device Guard: Security Services Running: Credential Guard
1619.description: This check verifies if Credential Guard is running as a security service for Device Guard. Credential Guard (value 1) uses virtualization-based security to isolate secrets, preventing credential theft attacks. It is recommended that Credential Guard is running. To resolve, ensure Credential Guard is enabled and actively running through Group Policy or system settings.

1618.title: Device Guard: Security Services Configured: HVCI
1618.description: This check verifies if Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity (HVCI) is configured as a security service for Device Guard. HVCI (value 2), also known as Memory Integrity, uses virtualization to isolate the Code Integrity service, protecting against malware that attempts to inject malicious code. It is recommended that HVCI is configured. To resolve, enable Memory Integrity (HVCI) through Group Policy or Windows Security settings.

1620.title: Device Guard: Security Services Running: HVCI
1620.description: This check verifies if Hypervisor-Enforced Code Integrity (HVCI) is running as a security service for Device Guard. HVCI (value 2), also known as Memory Integrity, uses virtualization to isolate the Code Integrity service, protecting against malware that attempts to inject malicious code. It is recommended that HVCI is running. To resolve, ensure Memory Integrity (HVCI) is enabled and actively running through Group Policy or Windows Security settings.

1623.title: Device Guard: Require UEFI Memory Attributes Table (Policy)
1623.description: This check verifies if Device Guard is configured to require the UEFI Memory Attributes Table (MAT). Requiring MAT (1) enhances the security of virtualization-based security by ensuring memory regions are properly protected. It is recommended to enable this policy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard\HVCIMATRequired` to `1`.

1621.title: Device Guard: Secure Launch Configuration (Policy)
1621.description: This check verifies if Device Guard's Secure Launch is configured. Secure Launch (1) helps protect the boot process by verifying the integrity of the system firmware and boot components. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this policy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard\ConfigureSystemGuardLaunch` to `1`.

1622.title: Device Guard: Windows Defender Application Control deployed (Policy)
1622.description: This check verifies if a Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) policy is deployed. Deploying a WDAC policy (1) restricts which applications can run on the system, providing strong protection against malware and unauthorized software. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to deploy a WDAC policy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard\DeployConfigCIPolicy` to `1` and ensure a valid WDAC policy is configured.

1630.title: Early Launch Antimalware: Boot-Start Driver Initialization Policy
1630.description: This check verifies the Early Launch Antimalware (ELAM) Boot-Start Driver Initialization Policy. Setting this to 'Good, unknown and bad' (3) ensures that ELAM drivers are initialized for all drivers, providing comprehensive protection against malicious drivers during the boot process. By default, it might be set to 'Good only' (0). It is recommended to set this policy to `3`. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Policies\EarlyLaunch\DriverLoadPolicy` to `3`.

1631.title: Group Policy: Process even if the Group Policy objects have not changed
1631.description: This check verifies if Group Policy objects are processed even if they have not changed. Forcing processing (1) can lead to unnecessary overhead. It is recommended to only process Group Policy objects when changes are detected (0) to optimize system performance. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Group Policy\{35378EAC-683F-11D2-A89A-00C04FBBCFA2}\NoBackgroundPolicy` to `0`.

1632.title: Group Policy: Do not apply during periodic background processing
1632.description: This check verifies if Group Policy is applied during periodic background processing. It is recommended to allow Group Policy to apply during periodic background processing (0) to ensure policies are consistently enforced. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Group Policy\{35378EAC-683F-11D2-A89A-00C04FBBCFA2}\NoGPOListChanges` is set to `0`.

1640.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off the Windows Messenger Customer Experience Improvement Program
1640.description: This check verifies if the Windows Messenger Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) is turned off. Disabling CEIP (2) prevents the system from sending usage data to Microsoft, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off this program. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Messenger\Client\CEIP` to `2`.

1641.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off downloading of print drivers over HTTP
1641.description: This check verifies if downloading print drivers over HTTP is turned off. Disabling this (1) prevents the use of unencrypted connections for driver downloads, reducing the risk of man-in-the-middle attacks and driver tampering. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off downloading print drivers over HTTP. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\DisableWebPnPDownload` to `1`.

1642.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off Windows Error Reporting 1
1642.description: This check verifies if Windows Error Reporting (WER) is turned off. While WER can help diagnose issues, disabling it (0) can prevent sensitive system information from being sent to Microsoft, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to turn off Windows Error Reporting. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\PCHealth\ErrorReporting\DoReport` to `0`.

1643.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off Windows Error Reporting 2
1643.description: This check verifies if Windows Error Reporting (WER) is turned off. While WER can help diagnose issues, disabling it (1) can prevent sensitive system information from being sent to Microsoft, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off Windows Error Reporting. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\Disabled` to `1`.

1644.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off Internet download for Web publishing and online ordering wizards
1644.description: This check verifies if Internet downloads for Web publishing and online ordering wizards are turned off. Disabling these downloads (1) can prevent the system from connecting to external services, reducing potential attack surfaces and improving security. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off these Internet downloads. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\NoWebServices` to `1`.

1645.title: Internet Communication Management: Internet Communication settings: Turn off Windows Customer Experience Improvement Program
1645.description: This check verifies if the Windows Customer Experience Improvement Program (CEIP) is turned off. Disabling CEIP (0) prevents the system from sending usage data to Microsoft, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to turn off this program. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\SQMClient\Windows\CEIPEnable` to `0`.

1650.title: Kernel DMA Protection: Enumeration policy for external devices incompatible with Kernel DMA Protection
1650.description: This check verifies the enumeration policy for external devices incompatible with Kernel DMA Protection. Setting this policy to 'Block all' (0) prevents potentially insecure devices from being connected, enhancing protection against DMA attacks. By default, it might be set to 'Allow all' (2). It is recommended to block all incompatible devices. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Kernel DMA Protection\DeviceEnumerationPolicy` to `0`.

1660.title: Logon: Turn on convenience PIN sign-in
1660.description: This check verifies if convenience PIN sign-in is turned off. While convenient, PINs can sometimes be less secure than strong passwords, especially if not backed by strong authentication mechanisms. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to turn off convenience PIN sign-in (0) to encourage stronger authentication methods. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\AllowDomainPINLogon` to `0`.

1661.title: Logon: Turn off app notifications on the lock screen
1661.description: This check verifies if app notifications are turned off on the lock screen. Displaying notifications on the lock screen (0) can expose sensitive information to unauthorized individuals. It is recommended to disable app notifications on the lock screen (1) to enhance privacy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\DisableLockScreenAppNotifications` to `1`.

1662.title: Logon: Do not display network selection UI
1662.description: This check verifies if the network selection UI is hidden on the logon screen. Hiding the network selection UI (1) can prevent users from connecting to unauthorized networks before logging in, reducing the risk of network-based attacks. By default, it might be displayed (0). It is recommended to hide the network selection UI. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\DontDisplayNetworkSelectionUI` to `1`.

1670.title: Mitigation Options: Untrusted Font Blocking
1670.description: This check verifies if Untrusted Font Blocking is enabled. Blocking untrusted fonts (1000000000000) helps protect against attacks that exploit vulnerabilities in font parsing, which can lead to arbitrary code execution. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable Untrusted Font Blocking. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\MitigationOptions\MitigationOptions_FontBocking` to `1000000000000`.

1680.title: OS Policies: Allow Clipboard synchronization across devices
1680.description: This check verifies if Clipboard synchronization across devices is disabled. Allowing clipboard synchronization (1) can lead to sensitive data being shared across devices, potentially exposing it to unauthorized access. It is recommended to disable this feature (0) for enhanced data privacy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\AllowCrossDeviceClipboard` to `0`.

1685.title: Sleep Settings: Require a password when a computer wakes (plugged in)
1685.description: This check verifies if a password is required when a computer wakes from sleep while plugged in. Requiring a password (1) prevents unauthorized access to the system if it is left unattended and goes to sleep. By default, it might not require a password (0). It is recommended to require a password. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power\PowerSettings\0e796bdb-100d-47d6-a2d5-f7d2daa51f51\ACSettingIndex` to `1`.

1686.title: Sleep Settings: Require a password when a computer wakes (on battery)
1686.description: This check verifies if a password is required when a computer wakes from sleep while on battery power. Requiring a password (1) prevents unauthorized access to the system if it is left unattended and goes to sleep. By default, it might not require a password (0). It is recommended to require a password. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power\PowerSettings\0e796bdb-100d-47d6-a2d5-f7d2daa51f51\DCSettingIndex` to `1`.

1687.title: Sleep Settings: Allow standby states (S1-S3) when sleeping (plugged in)
1687.description: This check verifies if standby states (S1-S3) are disallowed when the computer is sleeping and plugged in. Disallowing these states (0) can force the system into more secure sleep modes (e.g., S4/Hibernate) or prevent certain power-related attacks. By default, they might be allowed (1). It is recommended to disallow standby states S1-S3. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power\PowerSettings\abfc2519-3608-4c2a-94ea-171b0ed546ab\ACSettingIndex` to `0`.

1688.title: Sleep Settings: Allow standby states (S1-S3) when sleeping (on battery)
1688.description: This check verifies if standby states (S1-S3) are disallowed when the computer is sleeping and on battery power. Disallowing these states (0) can force the system into more secure sleep modes (e.g., S4/Hibernate) or prevent certain power-related attacks. By default, they might be allowed (1). It is recommended to disallow standby states S1-S3. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Power\PowerSettings\abfc2519-3608-4c2a-94ea-171b0ed546ab\DCSettingIndex` to `0`.

1690.title: Remote Assistance: Configure Offer Remote Assistance
1690.description: This check verifies if 'Offer Remote Assistance' is disabled. Enabling this (1) allows unsolicited remote assistance, which can be a security risk if not tightly controlled. It is recommended to disable unsolicited remote assistance (0). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\fAllowUnsolicited` to `0`.

1691.title: Remote Assistance: Configure Solicited Remote Assistance
1691.description: This check verifies if 'Solicited Remote Assistance' is disabled. While solicited remote assistance requires user consent, disabling it (0) can further reduce the attack surface, especially in environments where remote assistance is managed by other tools. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to disable solicited remote assistance. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services\fAllowToGetHelp` to `0`.

1692.title: Remote Procedure Call: Enable RPC Endpoint Mapper Client Authentication
1692.description: This check verifies if RPC Endpoint Mapper Client Authentication is enabled. Enabling authentication (1) for the RPC Endpoint Mapper helps prevent unauthorized clients from querying or interacting with RPC services, enhancing network security. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Rpc\EnableAuthEpResolution` to `1`.

1693.title: Remote Procedure Call: Restrict Unauthenticated RPC clients
1693.description: This check verifies if unauthenticated RPC clients are restricted. Setting this to 'Authenticated' (2) ensures that only authenticated clients can connect to RPC servers, significantly reducing the risk of unauthenticated attacks. By default, it might be set to 'None' (0). It is recommended to restrict unauthenticated RPC clients. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Rpc\RestrictRemoteClients` to `2`.

1694.title: Security Settings: Enable svchost.exe mitigation options
1694.description: This check verifies if svchost.exe mitigation options are enabled. Enabling these mitigations (1) helps protect critical system services running under svchost.exe from various exploitation techniques. By default, they might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable svchost.exe mitigation options. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SCMConfig\EnableSvchostMitigationPolicy` to `1`.

1695.title: Windows Performance PerfTrack: Enable/Disable PerfTrack
1695.description: This check verifies if Windows Performance PerfTrack is disabled. PerfTrack collects performance data, which, if enabled (1), could potentially expose system details. Disabling it (0) can reduce data collection and improve privacy. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to disable PerfTrack. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WDI\{9c5a40da-b965-4fc3-8781-88dd50a6299d}\ScenarioExecutionEnabled` to `0`.

1696.title: User Profiles: Turn off the advertising ID
1696.description: This check verifies if the advertising ID is turned off for user profiles. Disabling the advertising ID (1) enhances user privacy by preventing applications from using a unique identifier for targeted advertising. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off the advertising ID. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AdvertisingInfo\DisabledByGroupPolicy` to `1`.

1697.title: Time Providers: Enable Windows NTP Client
1697.description: This check verifies if the Windows NTP Client is enabled. Enabling the NTP client (1) ensures that the system's time is synchronized with a reliable time source, which is critical for security protocols (e.g., Kerberos) and accurate logging. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to enable the Windows NTP Client. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\W32time\TimeProviders\NtpClient\Enabled` to `1`.

1698.title: Time Providers: Enable Windows NTP Server
1698.description: This check verifies if the Windows NTP Server is disabled. Running an NTP server (1) can expose the system to time synchronization attacks or be used for amplification attacks if not properly secured. It is recommended to disable the Windows NTP Server (0) unless the system is specifically designated as a time server. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\W32time\TimeProviders\NtpServer\Enabled` is set to `0`.

1700.title: App Package Deployment: Allow a Windows app to share application data between users
1700.description: This check verifies if Windows apps are prevented from sharing application data between users. Allowing data sharing (1) can lead to privacy concerns and potential data leakage between user profiles. It is recommended to disable this feature (0) for enhanced user isolation and privacy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppModel\StateManager\AllowSharedLocalAppData` to `0`.

1701.title: App Privacy: Let Windows apps activate with voice while the system is locked
1701.description: This check verifies if Windows apps are prevented from activating with voice while the system is locked. Allowing voice activation (0) on the lock screen can pose a privacy risk and potentially allow unauthorized commands. It is recommended to disable this feature (2) to prevent apps from activating with voice above lock. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppPrivacy\LetAppsActivateWithVoiceAboveLock` to `2`.

1702.title: App runtime: Block launching Universal Windows apps with Windows Runtime API access from hosted content
1702.description: This check verifies if Universal Windows apps with Windows Runtime API access are blocked from launching from hosted content. Blocking this (1) enhances security by preventing potentially malicious hosted content from exploiting UWP apps with elevated privileges. By default, it might be allowed (0). It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\BlockHostedAppAccessWinRT` to `1`.

1703.title: Application Compatibility: Turn off Application Telemetry
1703.description: This check verifies if Application Telemetry is turned off. While telemetry can help improve application compatibility, disabling it (0) can prevent sensitive application usage data from being sent to Microsoft, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be enabled (1). It is recommended to turn off Application Telemetry. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\AppCompat\AITEnable` to `0`.

1704.title: AutoPlay Policies: Turn off Autoplay
1704.description: This check verifies if Autoplay is turned off for all drives. Autoplay (0) can automatically execute code from removable media, posing a significant security risk. It is recommended to disable Autoplay for all drive types (255) to prevent malware propagation. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\NoDriveTypeAutoRun` to `255`.

1705.title: AutoPlay Policies: Disallow Autoplay for non-volume devices
1705.description: This check verifies if Autoplay is disallowed for non-volume devices. Disallowing Autoplay (1) for devices like cameras or phones can prevent unintended execution of content and reduce the attack surface. By default, it might be allowed (0). It is recommended to disallow Autoplay for non-volume devices. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer\NoAutoplayfornonVolume` to `1`.

1706.title: AutoPlay Policies: Set the default behavior for AutoRun
1706.description: This check verifies if the default behavior for AutoRun is set to 'Do not execute any autorun commands'. Allowing AutoRun (0) can automatically execute code from removable media, posing a significant security risk. It is recommended to disable AutoRun (1) to prevent malware propagation. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\NoAutorun` to `1`.

1707.title: Biometrics: Allow the use of biometrics
1707.description: This check verifies if the use of biometrics is disallowed. While convenient, biometric authentication (1) can have security implications depending on the implementation and storage of biometric data. It is recommended to disallow the use of biometrics (0) unless specifically required and secured. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Biometrics\Enabled` to `0`.

1773.title: Biometrics: Facial Features: Configure enhanced anti-spoofing
1773.description: This check verifies if enhanced anti-spoofing is configured for facial biometric features. Enabling enhanced anti-spoofing (1) improves the security of facial recognition by making it harder for attackers to bypass authentication using photos or masks. It is recommended to enable this feature. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Biometrics\FacialFeatures\EnhancedAntiSpoofing` to `1`.

1708.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Volume status
1708.description: This check verifies the BitLocker encryption status of system volumes. It is critical that all volumes are 'FullyEncrypted' to protect data at rest from unauthorized access. If volumes are not encrypted, data can be easily compromised. To resolve, enable and complete BitLocker Drive Encryption for all system volumes, ensuring they reach a 'FullyEncrypted' state.

1761.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Choose drive encryption method and cipher strength (for operating system drives)
1761.description: This check verifies the BitLocker drive encryption method and cipher strength for operating system drives. It is recommended to use a strong encryption method like XTS-AES 256-bit (value 6) to provide robust data protection. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\EncryptionMethodWithXtsOs` is set to `6`.

1762.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Drive encryption method (for operating system drives)
1762.description: This check verifies the BitLocker drive encryption method for operating system drives. It is recommended to use a strong encryption method like XTS-AES 128-bit or higher (e.g., `XtsAes128`) to provide robust data protection. By default, it might be set to 'None'. To resolve, configure BitLocker to use `XtsAes128` or a stronger method for operating system drives.

1709.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Disable new DMA devices when this computer is locked
1709.description: This check verifies if new DMA devices are disabled when the computer is locked. Disabling new DMA devices (1) prevents direct memory access attacks when the system is locked, protecting sensitive data. By default, it might be enabled (0). It is recommended to disable new DMA devices when the computer is locked. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\DisableExternalDMAUnderLock` to `1`.

1710.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Allow Secure Boot for integrity validation
1710.description: This check verifies if Secure Boot is allowed for BitLocker integrity validation on operating system drives. Allowing Secure Boot (1) enhances the integrity of the boot process, ensuring that only trusted components are loaded before BitLocker unlocks the drive. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to allow Secure Boot for integrity validation. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\OSAllowSecureBootForIntegrity` to `1`.

1711.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup
1711.description: This check verifies if additional authentication is required at startup for BitLocker-protected operating system drives. Requiring additional authentication (1) (e.g., PIN or USB key) significantly strengthens protection against unauthorized access, even if the TPM is compromised. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to require additional authentication at startup. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseAdvancedStartup` to `1`.

1715.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup: Allow BitLocker without a compatible TPM
1715.description: This check verifies if BitLocker is prevented from being used without a compatible TPM on operating system drives. Allowing BitLocker without a TPM (1) significantly weakens its security, as the encryption key is not hardware-protected. It is recommended to disallow BitLocker without a compatible TPM (0). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\EnableBDEWithNoTPM` to `0`.

1716.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup: Configure TPM startup
1716.description: This check verifies if BitLocker is configured to use the TPM for startup authentication on operating system drives. Using the TPM (0) provides hardware-based protection for the encryption key. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseTPM` is set to `0`.

1717.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup: Configure TPM startup PIN
1717.description: This check verifies if BitLocker is configured to require a TPM startup PIN for operating system drives. Requiring a PIN (1) in addition to the TPM provides multi-factor authentication at boot, significantly increasing security against physical attacks. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to configure a TPM startup PIN. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseTPMPIN` to `1`.

1718.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup: Configure TPM startup key
1718.description: This check verifies if BitLocker is configured to require a TPM startup key for operating system drives. Requiring a startup key (0) in addition to the TPM provides multi-factor authentication at boot, significantly increasing security against physical attacks. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseTPMKey` is set to `0`.

1719.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Require additional authentication at startup: Configure TPM startup key and PIN
1719.description: This check verifies if BitLocker is configured to require both a TPM startup key and PIN for operating system drives. Requiring both (0) provides the strongest multi-factor authentication at boot, significantly increasing security against physical attacks. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseTPMKeyPIN` is set to `0`.

1712.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Allow enhanced PINs for startup
1712.description: This check verifies if enhanced PINs are allowed for BitLocker startup on operating system drives. Allowing enhanced PINs (1) enables the use of more complex and longer PINs, increasing the strength of pre-boot authentication. By default, it might be disabled (0). It is recommended to allow enhanced PINs. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\UseEnhancedPin` to `1`.

1713.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Configure use of hardware-based encryption for operating system drives
1713.description: This check verifies if hardware-based encryption is configured for BitLocker on operating system drives. While hardware encryption can be faster, it can also have security implications depending on the drive's firmware. It is recommended to use software-based encryption (0) unless hardware encryption is thoroughly vetted and trusted. The default setting already aligns with the recommendation. To resolve, ensure the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\OSHardwareEncryption` is set to `0`.

1763.title: BitLocker Drive Encryption: Operating System Drives: Configure minimum PIN length for startup
1763.description: This check verifies if a minimum PIN length is configured for BitLocker startup on operating system drives. Requiring a minimum PIN length of 8 characters or more significantly increases the strength of pre-boot authentication against brute-force attacks. It is recommended to set the minimum PIN length to at least 8. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\FVE\MinimumPIN` to `8` or higher.

1720.title: Cloud Content: Do not show Windows tips
1720.description: This check verifies if Windows tips are disabled. Disabling Windows tips (1) can reduce unnecessary network communication and potential exposure to external content, enhancing privacy and reducing distractions. By default, they might be enabled (0). It is recommended to disable Windows tips. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent\DisableSoftLanding` to `1`.

1721.title: Cloud Content: Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences
1721.description: This check verifies if Microsoft consumer experiences are turned off. Disabling consumer experiences (1) can reduce unwanted applications, advertisements, and network activity, improving system performance and security. By default, they might be enabled (0). It is recommended to turn off Microsoft consumer experiences. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CloudContent\DisableWindowsConsumerFeatures` to `1`.

1722.title: Credential User Interface: Do not display the password reveal button
1722.description: This check verifies if the password reveal button is hidden in the credential user interface. Hiding the reveal button (1) prevents shoulder surfing and accidental exposure of passwords, enhancing security in shared environments. By default, it might be displayed (0). It is recommended to hide the password reveal button. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CredUI\DisablePasswordReveal` to `1`.

1724.title: Credential User Interface: Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation
1724.description: This check verifies if administrator accounts are prevented from being enumerated on elevation. Enumerating administrator accounts (1) can provide attackers with valuable information for privilege escalation. It is recommended to disable the enumeration of administrator accounts (0) to obscure potential targets. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\CredUI\EnumerateAdministrators` to `0`.

1725.title: Data Collection and Preview Builds: Allow Diagnostic Data
1725.description: This check verifies the level of diagnostic data allowed to be sent to Microsoft. It is recommended to set the diagnostic data level to 'Basic' (1) or lower to minimize the amount of potentially sensitive information collected, enhancing privacy. By default, it might be set to 'Enhanced' (2). To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection\AllowTelemetry` to `1`.

1726.title: Data Collection and Preview Builds: Allow device name to be sent in Windows diagnostic data
1726.description: This check verifies if the device name is prevented from being sent in Windows diagnostic data. Sending the device name (1) can expose identifiable information. It is recommended to disable sending the device name (0) to enhance privacy. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DataCollection\AllowDeviceNameInTelemetry` to `0`.

1727.title: Delivery Optimization: Download Mode
1727.description: This check verifies the Delivery Optimization download mode. Setting the download mode to 'HTTP only' (99) prevents the system from sharing updates with other devices on the local network or the internet, reducing network exposure and potential for data leakage. By default, it might be set to 'LAN' (1). It is recommended to set the download mode to `99`. To resolve, set the registry value `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization\DODownloadMode` to `99`.

1728.title: Event Log Service: Application: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)
1728.description: This setting controls the maximum size of the Application event log file in kilobytes. A small log size can lead to important security or system events being overwritten quickly, hindering incident response and troubleshooting. The default size is 4096 KB. To resolve this, set the registry value `MaxSize` under `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog\Application` to `32768` (KB) or higher. This can be configured via Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Event Log Service -> Application) or directly in the registry.

1729.title: Event Log Service: Security: Specify the maximum log file size (KB)
1729.description: This setting controls the maximum size of the Security event log file in kilobytes. A small log size can lead to critical security events being overwritten quickly, hindering incident response and forensic analysis. The default size is 4096 KB. To resolve this, set the registry value `MaxSize` under `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog\Security` to `196608` (KB) or higher. These features are typically unnecessary on server operating systems and disabling them can reduce resource consumption and potential attack surface. The default value is 1 (enabled). To resolve this, ensure the registry value `AllowGameDVR` under `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR` is set to `0` (disabled). This can be configured via Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting) or directly in the registry.

1748.title: Windows Ink Workspace: Allow Windows Ink Workspace
1748.description: This setting controls whether the Windows Ink Workspace is allowed. This feature is designed for pen input and is generally not required or desired on server operating systems. Disabling it can reduce unnecessary components. The default value is 1 (allowed). To resolve this, ensure the registry value `AllowWindowsInkWorkspace` under `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsInkWorkspace` is set to `0` (disallowed). This can be configured via Group Policy (Computer Configuration -> Administrative Templates -> Windows Components -> Windows Ink Workspace) or directly in the registry.

1749.title: Windows Installer: Always install with elevated privileges
1749.description: This setting controls whether Windows Installer packages are always installed with elevated system privileges. When enabled (value 1), any user can install applications with system privileges, which is a significant security risk as it allows for privilege escalation. The recommended value of `0` (disabled) ensures that installations run with the user's privileges, preventing malicious users from exploiting the installer to gain system-level access. Ensure the registry value `AlwaysInstallElevated` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer` is set to `0`.

1750.title: Windows Installer: Allow user control over installs
1750.description: This setting allows users to control certain aspects of Windows Installer installations. When enabled (value 1), users might be able to modify installation options that could bypass security restrictions or install unwanted components. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents users from overriding installation settings, ensuring that installations adhere to predefined security policies and configurations. This reduces the risk of users introducing vulnerabilities or unwanted software. Set the registry value `EnableUserControl` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer` to `0`.

1751.title: Windows Installer: Prevent Internet Explorer security prompt for Windows Installer scripts
1751.description: This setting controls whether Windows Installer scripts are prevented from triggering Internet Explorer security prompts. When enabled (value 1), it can suppress security warnings, potentially allowing malicious scripts to run without user intervention. Setting this to `0` (disabled) ensures that Internet Explorer security prompts are displayed for Windows Installer scripts, providing a layer of protection against potentially harmful scripts. Set the registry value `SafeForScripting` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer` to `0`.

1752.title: Windows Logon Options: Sign-in and lock last interactive user automatically after a restart
1752.description: This setting controls whether the last interactive user is automatically signed in and locked after a system restart. When disabled (value 0), the system will automatically sign in the last user, which can expose sensitive information or allow unauthorized access if the system is physically compromised before the lock screen activates. Setting this to `1` (enabled) prevents automatic sign-in, requiring explicit user authentication after a restart, thereby enhancing security and protecting user sessions. Set the registry value `DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System` to `1`.

1770.title: Windows Installer: Disable Co-Installer (USB AutoInstall)
1770.description: This setting disables the use of co-installers, which are often used for USB AutoInstall functionality. Co-installers can sometimes be a vector for installing unsigned or malicious drivers. Setting this to `1` (enabled) prevents the automatic installation of drivers via co-installers, reducing the risk of unauthorized or vulnerable driver installations and enhancing system integrity. Set the registry value `DisableCoInstallers` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Device Installer` to `1`.

1753.title: WinRM Client: Allow Basic authentication
1753.description: This setting controls whether WinRM Client Basic authentication is permitted. When enabled (value 1), it allows less secure methods like Basic authentication, which can expose credentials or data to eavesdropping and replay attacks. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents the use of Basic authentication, forcing more secure communication protocols and authentication methods, thereby significantly enhancing the security of WinRM communications. Set the registry value `AllowBasic` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Client` to `0`.

1754.title: WinRM Client: Allow unencrypted traffic

1755.title: WinRM Client: Disallow Digest authentication

1756.title: WinRM Service: Allow remote server management through WinRM

1759.title: WinRM Service: Disallow WinRM from storing RunAs credentials
1759.description: This setting controls whether WinRM is allowed to store RunAs credentials. When disabled (value 0), WinRM can store credentials, which poses a security risk if the system is compromised, as these credentials could be exfiltrated. Setting this to `1` (enabled) prevents WinRM from storing RunAs credentials, forcing users to provide credentials for each operation or use more secure credential management, thereby reducing the risk of credential theft. Set the registry value `DisableRunAs` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Service` to `1`.

1760.title: Windows Remote Shell: Allow Remote Shell Access
1760.description: This setting controls whether Windows Remote Shell remote shell access is permitted. When enabled (value 1), it allows less secure methods like remote shell access, which can expose credentials or data to eavesdropping and replay attacks. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents the use of remote shell access, forcing more secure communication protocols and authentication methods, thereby significantly enhancing the security of WinRM communications. Set the registry value `AllowRemoteShellAccess` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WinRM\Service\WinRS` to `0`.

2000.title: File Explorer: Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen
2000.description: This setting configures Windows Defender SmartScreen, a feature that helps protect users from malicious websites and downloads. When enabled (value 1), SmartScreen actively checks files and websites, providing warnings or blocking access to known threats. Disabling it (value 0) leaves the system vulnerable to phishing attacks, malware downloads, and other web-based threats. The recommended value of `1` ensures that SmartScreen is active, providing a crucial layer of defense against online threats. Ensure the registry value `EnableSmartScreen` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System` is set to `1`.

2001.title: File Explorer: Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen to warn and prevent bypass
2001.description: This setting configures the behavior of Windows Defender SmartScreen, specifically how it handles potentially malicious content. The 'Warn' setting allows users to bypass warnings, potentially exposing them to threats. The 'Block' setting (recommended) prevents users from bypassing SmartScreen warnings for untrusted files and websites, providing stronger protection against malware and phishing attacks. This ensures that users cannot easily override security decisions. Set the registry value `ShellSmartScreenLevel` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System` to `Block`.

2105.title: Turn on PowerShell Module Logging
2105.description: This setting controls PowerShell Module Logging. When disabled (value 0), PowerShell activity is not fully logged, making it difficult to detect and investigate malicious activity. Enabling this (value 1) provides detailed logs of PowerShell commands, script blocks, or transcripts, which are crucial for security monitoring, threat detection, and forensic analysis, significantly enhancing visibility into potential attacks. Set the registry value `EnableModuleLogging` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ModuleLogging` to `1`.

2106.title: Turn on PowerShell Module Logging - Module Names
2106.description: This setting specifies which PowerShell modules should be logged when PowerShell Module Logging is enabled. Setting this to `*` (all) ensures that all PowerShell modules are logged. This provides comprehensive visibility into all module-related activity, which is essential for detecting and investigating sophisticated attacks that leverage PowerShell modules. Set the registry value `ModuleNames` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ModuleLogging\ModuleNames` to `*`.

2103.title: Disable PowerShell version 2
2103.description: This setting controls the 'Disable PowerShell version 2' Windows Optional Feature, specifically 'MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2'. When 'Enabled', this feature is active. For example, PowerShell version 2 is an older, less secure version that lacks many of the security features and logging capabilities present in newer versions (e.g., v5+). Keeping it enabled provides an attack vector for adversaries to execute scripts without enhanced logging and security protections. Setting this to 'Disabled' disables the feature, removing this legacy component and forcing scripts to run on more secure and auditable versions, significantly improving the system's security posture. Disable the Windows Optional Feature `MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2`. This can be done via PowerShell using `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2 -Remove`.
