This can be done via PowerShell using `Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root -Remove`.

2200.title: LSA Protection
2200.description: This setting enables LSA Protection (Protected Process Light), which helps protect the Local Security Authority (LSA) process from unauthorized code injection and credential theft. When disabled (value 0), the LSA process is more vulnerable to attacks that aim to extract sensitive credentials. Setting this to `1` (enabled) hardens the LSA process, making it significantly more difficult for attackers to compromise and steal credentials like NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets. Set the registry value `RunAsPPL` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa` to `1`. A system restart is required.

2201.title: Lsass.exe audit mode
2201.description: This setting configures the audit level for `lsass.exe`, the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service. Setting an audit level of `8` enables verbose auditing for `lsass.exe`, which can provide valuable insights into potential attacks targeting the LSA process, such as credential dumping attempts. This enhanced logging aids in detection and forensic analysis. Set the registry value `AuditLevel` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\LSASS.exe` to `8`.

2202.title: NetBT NodeType configuration
2202.description: This setting configures the NetBT (NetBIOS over TCP/IP) node type, which determines how NetBIOS name resolution occurs. A node type of `0` (B-node) relies on broadcasts, which can be inefficient and susceptible to spoofing. Setting this to `2` (P-node) or `4` (H-node) forces the use of WINS servers for name resolution, reducing broadcast traffic and mitigating risks associated with NetBIOS name spoofing and enumeration on local networks. Set the registry value `NodeType` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NetBT\Parameters` to `2`.

2203.title: WDigest Authentication
2203.description: This setting controls whether WDigest authentication stores plaintext credentials in memory. When enabled (value 1), WDigest stores user credentials in an easily recoverable plaintext format in the LSASS process memory, making them highly vulnerable to credential dumping attacks. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents WDigest from storing plaintext credentials, significantly reducing the risk of credential theft and protecting against common post-exploitation techniques. Set the registry value `UseLogonCredential` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest` to `0`. A system restart is required.

2209.title: Enable Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP)
2209.description: This setting controls Structured Exception Handling Overwrite Protection (SEHOP). When enabled (value 1), it disables SEHOP, making the system vulnerable to exploits that overwrite exception handlers to execute arbitrary code. Setting this to `0` (disabled) enables SEHOP, which validates the integrity of exception handler chains, providing a critical defense against a class of memory corruption exploits. Set the registry value `DisableExceptionChainValidation` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\kernel` to `0`.

2210.title: Limits print driver installation to Administrators
2210.description: This setting restricts the installation of print drivers to administrators only. When disabled (value 0), non-administrative users can install print drivers, which has historically been a vector for privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution (e.g., PrintNightmare vulnerabilities). Setting this to `1` (enabled) ensures that only authorized administrators can install drivers, significantly reducing the attack surface related to printer services and enhancing system security. Set the registry value `RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators` at `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint` to `1`.

2211.title: Configure RPC packet level privacy setting for incoming connections
2211.description: This setting configures the RPC packet level privacy for incoming print connections. When disabled (value 0), RPC communications for printing may not be encrypted, making them vulnerable to eavesdropping and tampering. Setting this to `1` (enabled) enforces packet-level privacy (encryption) for RPC communications, protecting sensitive print job data and credentials from interception and ensuring secure communication with print servers. Set the registry value `RpcAuthnLevelPrivacyEnabled` at `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print` to `1`.

2212.title: Manage processing of Queue-specific files
2212.description: This setting manages the processing of queue-specific files for printers. When disabled (value 0), it may allow for less secure handling of print-related files, potentially leading to vulnerabilities. Setting this to `1` (enabled) enforces a more secure policy for handling queue-specific files, reducing the risk of malicious file execution or privilege escalation through print services. Set the registry value `CopyFilesPolicy` at `HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers` to `1`.

2204.title: MSS: (SafeDllSearchMode) Enable Safe DLL search mode (recommended)
2204.description: This setting enables Safe DLL Search Mode, which changes the order in which Windows searches for DLLs. When disabled (value 0), Windows might search in less secure locations first, making it vulnerable to DLL hijacking attacks. Setting this to `1` (enabled) prioritizes secure system directories for DLL searches, significantly mitigating the risk of malicious DLLs being loaded instead of legitimate ones. Set the registry value `SafeDLLSearchMode` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager` to `1`.

2205.title: MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting IPv6) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)
2205.description: This setting controls IPv6 IP source routing, which allows the sender of a packet to specify the route it takes. When enabled (value 1 for IPv4, 0 for IPv6), it can be exploited for packet spoofing and bypassing network security controls. Setting this to `2` (highest protection) disables IP source routing, preventing attackers from manipulating network routes and enhancing network security against spoofing attacks. Set the registry value `DisableIPSourceRouting` at `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip6\Parameters` to `2`.

2206.title: MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level (protects against packet spoofing)
2206.description: This setting controls IPv4 IP source routing, which allows the sender of a packet to specify the route it takes. When enabled (value 1 for IPv4, 0 for IPv6), it can be exploited for packet spoofing and bypassing network security controls. Setting this to `2` (highest protection) disables IP source routing, preventing attackers from manipulating network routes and enhancing network security against spoofing attacks. Set the registry value `DisableIPSourceRouting` at `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters` to `2`.

2207.title: MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes
2207.description: This setting controls whether the system allows ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes. When enabled (value 1), it can allow malicious actors to redirect network traffic by sending forged ICMP redirect messages, leading to man-in-the-middle attacks or denial of service. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents ICMP redirects from altering routing tables, protecting the system from route manipulation and ensuring traffic flows through legitimate paths. Set the registry value `EnableICMPRedirect` at `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters` to `0`.

2208.title: MSS: (NoNameReleaseOnDemand) Allow the computer to ignore NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers
2208.description: This setting controls whether the computer ignores NetBIOS name release requests except from WINS servers. When disabled (value 0), the system may respond to unsolicited NetBIOS name release requests, which can be exploited in NetBIOS spoofing attacks. Setting this to `1` (enabled) ensures that the system only accepts name release requests from trusted WINS servers, mitigating the risk of NetBIOS name service poisoning and related attacks. Set the registry value `NoNameReleaseOnDemand` at `HKLM:\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netbt\Parameters` to `1`.

2400.title: XblGameSave Standby Task
2400.description: This setting controls the 'XblGameSave Standby Task' scheduled task, specifically 'XblGameSaveTask'. For servers or systems not used for gaming or specific consumer features, this task is unnecessary and consumes system resources. While not a direct security vulnerability, unnecessary services and tasks increase the attack surface and can introduce potential stability or performance issues. Setting this to 'Disabled' (Disabled) reduces the system's attack surface, conserves resources, and removes an unnecessary component, aligning with the principle of least functionality for server hardening. Disable the scheduled task named `XblGameSaveTask`. This can be done via Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) or using PowerShell: `Disable-ScheduledTask -TaskName "XblGameSaveTask"`.

2411.title: Disable mDNS in Dnscache service
2411.description: This setting disables mDNS (multicast DNS) in the Dnscache service. When enabled (value 1), mDNS can expose internal network information and be susceptible to spoofing attacks. Setting this to `0` (disabled) prevents the Dnscache service from using mDNS, reducing the attack surface and preventing potential information disclosure or spoofing vulnerabilities. Set the registry value `EnableMDNS` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Dnscache\Parameters` to `0`.

2401.title: Print Spooler (Spooler)
2401.description: This setting controls the startup type of the 'Print Spooler' service. When set to `2` (Automatic) or `3` (Manual), the service can run, potentially exposing vulnerabilities or consuming unnecessary resources if the service is not required. Setting this to `4` (Disabled) prevents the service from starting, which is a critical hardening measure for services like Print Spooler or Xbox services that are often unnecessary on servers and have a history of security vulnerabilities. Disabling unnecessary services reduces the attack surface and improves system security. Set the registry value `Start` at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Spooler` to `4` (Disabled).

2402.title: Print Spooler (Spooler) (Service Startup type)

2300.title: HardeningKitty-Block-TCP-NetBIOS
2300.description: This firewall rule blocks inbound TCP traffic on ports 137, 138, and 139. Without this rule, services listening on these ports are exposed, which can be exploited for information gathering or various attacks, especially if the services are not strictly required. Creating this rule prevents external and internal attackers from interacting with these services, reducing the attack surface and mitigating risks associated with enumeration and exploitation. Create a new Windows Defender Firewall rule to block inbound TCP traffic on ports 137, 138, and 139. The rule should be configured as: Direction: Inbound, Action: Block, Protocol: TCP, Local Ports: 137, 138, 139.
